notes: 1.16: the 2.0.3 update: the admin card moved into admin.js, which ships with the game, so ` opens it as its own panel in the installed game whenever you are on the server as Tree (your other PC uses the game's own connection, which the server knows is you); the dev panel on the key PC shows the same card, and your two Trees can't kick, ban or mute each other. 1.15: the 2.0.2 update: Tree on two PCs. Your main PC (with the admin key) and one more PC can both be Tree, even at the same time; the other PC gets in with the Tree password set in the admin card (TREE ON 2 PCS, which also shows and frees the two slots), and the name box asks for it only when you join as Tree from a PC that isn't one of yours. Wrong passwords are slowed down. 1.14: the 2.0.1 update: announcements come in two kinds, Quick (only whoever is on now) and News (everyone, joiners and the main menu), each up for as long as you say or until you take it down, stacked up to 5 at the top with the older ones moving up, and an Up now list in the admin card to take any down; T chat no longer pauses the game and chat never gets stuck on screen; names are asked for once and saved, nobody can be on with the same name, a name stays with whoever used it for 30 days, Tree and staff-sounding names need the admin key, and the admin card can free a name. 1.13: the 2.0.0 update: Join public server on the main menu, an admin card in the dev panel (only with your key in admin.key.js, which git ignores) for announcements everyone sees as a banner and on the menu, the message of the day, mute, kick and ban, a Cloudflare server (server/, at treesim4-server.jacksongamer25.workers.dev) where players on the same island see each other walk, swing and lead their pets, with names overhead, chat on T and a player list on Tab; and pets: Sly's Black Market, a shady cart beside the enchanting table on every island, sells three cases (Burlap Sack, Smuggler's Crate, Reaper's Coffer) that spin out one of 24 pets in five rarities, with a 2.5% chance of a shiny; pets follow you, each with a perk (axe damage, logs, cash, speed, mutation luck, log reach, or biting the tree you're chopping), duplicates add stars, P shows your pets, and a third pet can follow you from Rebirth 8. 1.12: two new casino wings: the Hi-Lo Wing (Hi-Lo, Card War, Baccarat) and the Keno Lounge (Keno, Over/Under 7 dice, Coin Flip), through arches either side of the entrance, each with dealers, signs and a chandelier; and the casino fixed (these were in 1.8.0 too, on the Iceberg): marble pillars no longer grow through the Hi-Lo table and the Keno kiosk, the Hi-Lo dealer keeps his head when you walk near, and Plinko shows its board. 1.11: fixed things you moved with Built-ins landing on their neighbours (a bed in the forge, the forge's name following the bed) after 1.10 took the tent away: the tent's place is kept, moves now remember what they moved and find it again, and Put everything back clears an island's moves; a swapped camp building stands right behind its keeper; typing an island's text, ticket or menu look no longer rebuilds the island (its name and camp name rebuild once when you leave the box); Plinko's board shows (its frame was in front of it); things moved with Built-ins turn all the way round (they stopped at 90°); a big bed of your own is solid and you can sleep from anywhere round its edge. 1.10: the enchanting table stands on the ground on every Studio island (it used the last island's ground), and ✥ Built-ins can move, turn, size or hide it; floating names on anything: placed things get size and height, and anything the game built (the forge, BED, the Ferryman, the casino, the enchanting table) can have its names changed, hidden or added; names no longer vanish when an island rebuilds; with ✥ Built-ins on you can still click what you placed (a portal); the usual tent is an A-frame now, and a bed of your own stands alone. 1.9: a Bed slot in the Islands tab's ARCHITECTURE: your model replaces the bed you sleep in (a small model picked as the bed hut counts too), and ✦ Restyle with Claude gives the casino a new look any time, from the island or what you describe. 1.8: the casino moves by itself to your newest island and is re-skinned for it, outside and in: its name and sign line, colours, a spire, dome, crown or flat roof, which side it stands on, and the hall's wallpaper, carpet, trim and chandeliers. Ask Claude designs one for every island; without one it takes the island's own colours. Fixed: the shop menu no longer clashes with the casino's. 1.7: Ask Claude can invent a whole island: its own architecture (the bed hut, forge, trading post and witch's hut rebuilt in one style), shops with their own keepers, buildings and things to buy, models, landmarks, trees, animals and people, three requests at a time; each island gets its own menu look (colours, a heading font, corners), always readable. Shops work by hand too (🛒 Shop in the Place tab, or the Islands tab), and you can swap any camp building for one of your props. 1.6: ⟳ Sync brings in what's on GitHub (releases and Studio updates) and keeps your own work: islands, trees, props, animals, people and placed things from both sides are kept, and islands already on GitHub keep their rebirths while yours move after them, trees and all; npm run studio:update does the same from a terminal, then installs and starts the Studio. You can walk onto the docks again: the Iceberg's arrivals and Rebirth 6 docks, and every Studio island's. 1.5: the People Maker (new kinds of people: hair, hats, beards, faces, clothes, what they hold and say, or ask Claude; islands get residents too), the top bar wraps instead of pushing Release and Play off screen, and "Gives off real light" switches off properly instead of piling up. 1.4: your work is also kept in Documents/Tree Sim 4 Studio (with dated backups), and after an update or a fresh download the Studio offers to bring it back; Ask Claude can do anything with an island: new outlines (long, lobed), walkable islands joined by bridges, new buildings it builds from parts, and the game's props put around it; you can make all of that by hand too. 1.3: move, turn, resize or hide anything the game built (beds, stalls, signs, rocks), with its collisions, label and press-F spot; sculpt your islands' ground with Raise, Lower, Flatten and Erase brushes. 1.2: your trees grow (the Studio shows every tree an island can grow; an island can let every tree grow from the start), Unused and On islands tree lists, trees in the Islands tab with how common each one is, the ecosystem (animals, ground cover, fireflies), the Animal Maker (parts with legs, wings and tails that move, or ask Claude), each island's own materials and axes, and Ask Claude invents all of it with the island. 1.1: the Prop Maker, island features, Ask Claude for islands, your own themes
